lemmas.proof_markdown:
KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives the affine point–line mixing inequality with normalized error

$$
\frac{\sqrt{\mu(X)\tau}}{\sqrt{p+1}}.
$$

The first numerical hypothesis and $d>100$ imply

$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{p+1}}\le \frac{k}{4p}.
$$

Applying the minimum-degree argument of KTZ Lemma 6.2 to the point and line sides of $G$ therefore gives

$$
\mu(X),\tau\ge \frac{k}{4p}.
$$

Since $t=\tau p(p+1)$, the line-side estimate also gives $t\ge k(p+1)/4$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime and let $d$ be an integer satisfying $100<d<p$. Let $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$, and assign to every affine line $L\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^2$ a polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most $d$. Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected subgraph of the accepted-incidence graph with minimum degree $k$, where an incidence $(x,L)$ is accepted when $P_L(x)=f(x)$. Put

$$
t=|T|,\qquad \mu(X)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\qquad \tau=\frac{t}{p(p+1)},\qquad C_*=2^{40}.
$$

Assume

$$
k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2.
$$

Then

$$
\mu(X)\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.
$$

In particular, $t\ge k(p+1)/4$.
lemmas.title: Component Measures

dependencies: uniqueness of the affine line through two points
lemmas.proof_markdown:
Select every line of $T$ independently with probability $8/k$. For a fixed $L\in T$ and $x\in N_G(L)$, at least $k-1$ other accepted lines of $G$ pass through $x$. Thus $x$ is reached with probability at least

$$
1-\left(1-\frac{8}{k}\right)^{k-1}\ge\frac34.
$$

For distinct points of $L$, the relevant sets of other lines are disjoint, because two distinct points have only one common affine line, namely $L$. Their reach indicators are therefore independent. A Chernoff bound gives

$$
\Pr\left[\text{at most half of }N_G(L)\text{ is reached}\right]
 \le e^{-\deg_G(L)/24}
 \le e^{-k/24}.
$$

The numerical hypotheses imply $k\gg\log p$, so a union bound over fewer than $2p^2$ affine lines succeeds. A second Chernoff bound simultaneously places the sample size between half and twice its expectation $8t/k$. Hence a deterministic choice of $R$ has the asserted coverage and size. By P1,

$$
|R|\ge\frac{4t}{k}\ge p+1.
$$
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1, there exists a set $R\subseteq T$ such that

$$
\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k},
$$

and, for every $L\in T$,

$$
\left|\left\{x\in N_G(L):\exists\,M\in R\setminus\{L\}\text{ with }(x,M)\in E\right\}\right|
>\frac12\deg_G(L).
$$

Moreover, $|R|\ge p+1$ and $|R|=\Theta(\tau p^2/k)$ with absolute implied constants.
lemmas.title: Reaching Family

lemmas.proof_markdown:
From the definition of $D$ and the bounds on $r$ supplied by P2,

$$
D^2>256dr,
$$

and

$$
D^2\le1024dr\le\frac{16384dt}{k}\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k}.
$$

The hypothesis $k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2$ therefore gives $D/k<1/5000$. Since $r\ge p+1$ by P2 and every line vertex has degree at most $p$, one has

$$
D<k\le p<r.
$$

KTZ Lemma 2.2 supplies at least $D^3/(64d)$ eligible monomials of weighted degree at most $D$. Each identity imposed by a selected line contributes at most $D+1$ homogeneous coefficient constraints. Since

$$
\frac{D^3}{64d}>r(D+1),
$$

there is a nonzero interpolant satisfying all $r$ identities.

If the interpolant were independent of $Z$, each of the $r>D$ distinct selected affine lines would be a linear factor of a nonzero polynomial of degree at most $D$, which is impossible. The eligible monomials have $Z$-exponent zero or a positive $Z$-exponent not divisible by $p$; hence $Z$-dependence implies that the formal derivative $A_Z$ is nonzero. Choosing an interpolant of minimum weighted degree and applying the reductions in KTZ Lemmas 2.3 and 2.5 makes $A$ squarefree.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1 and P2, put $r=|R|$ and

$$
D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\right\rfloor+1\right).
$$

There exists a nonzero squarefree polynomial $A\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$ for weights $(1,1,d)$ such that

$$
A_Z\not\equiv0
$$

and

$$
A(M(s),P_M(s))\equiv0\qquad\text{for every }M\in R,
$$

where $M(s)$ is an affine parametrization of $M$. Moreover,

$$
D^2>256dr,
\qquad
D^2\le1024dr\le\frac{16384dt}{k}\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k},
\qquad
\frac{D}{k}<\frac1{5000},
$$

so $D<k\le p<r$ and $D=O\!\left(\sqrt{d\tau p^2/k}\right)$.
lemmas.title: Trivariate Explainer

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Fix $L\in T$. If an accepted point $x\in N_G(L)$ is reached by some $M\in R\setminus\{L\}$, then

$$
P_L(x)=f(x)=P_M(x).
$$

The sampled-line identity gives $A(x,P_M(x))=0$, and hence $A(x,P_L(x))=0$. By P2, this holds at more than half of the accepted neighbors of $L$, so the univariate polynomial

$$
s\longmapsto A(L(s),P_L(s))
$$

has more than $k/2>D$ distinct roots. Its degree is at most $D$, and it must therefore vanish identically. This argument applies to every $L\in T$ and incurs no averaging or Markov loss.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$, $R$, $A$, and $D$ satisfy the hypotheses and conclusions of P2 and P3. Then, for every $L\in T$ and every affine parametrization $L(s)$,

$$
A(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0.
$$
lemmas.title: Linewise Extension

lemmas.proof_markdown:
At most $D$ affine lines can make $H(L(s))$ vanish identically, because each such line contributes a distinct linear factor of $H$ and $\deg H\le D$. On any other line, the identity from P4 reads

$$
H(L(s))B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0.
$$

Since $\mathbb{F}_p[s]$ is an integral domain and $H(L(s))$ is nonzero, exact polynomial division gives $B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0$.

The quotient $B$ is squarefree and has degree below $p$. Since $\mathbb{F}_p$ is perfect, an irreducible factor whose three formal partial derivatives all vanish would be a nontrivial power with exponent $p$, which is impossible here. KTZ Lemma 2.4 therefore supplies a formal directional derivative $\mathcal{D}$ satisfying $\gcd(B,\mathcal{D}B)=1$.

KTZ Lemma 2.6 applies the relevant resultant to bound by $D(D-1)$ the lines on whose polynomial graphs both $B$ and $\mathcal{D}B$ vanish identically. On every other nontrivial line, the restricted derivative is a nonzero univariate polynomial of degree at most $D$, so it has at most $D$ accepted zeros. The trivial and degenerate lines contribute at most

$$
pD+pD(D-1)=pD^2
$$

edges, and all remaining lines contribute at most $Dt$. Thus $|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+Dt$. The argument uses a resultant rather than a discriminant.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P4, write

$$
A=\sum_j a_j(X,Y)Z^j,
\qquad
H(X,Y)=\gcd_j a_j(X,Y),
\qquad
B=A/H.
$$

Then $B$ is squarefree, has total degree less than $p$, and satisfies

$$
B(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0
$$

for every $L\in T$ such that $H(L(s))\not\equiv0$. There exists a formal directional derivative $\mathcal{D}$ such that

$$
\gcd(B,\mathcal{D}B)=1.
$$

Define

$$
T_{\mathrm{triv}}=\{L\in T:H(L(s))\equiv0\}
$$

and

$$
T_{\mathrm{deg}}=
\left\{L\in T\setminus T_{\mathrm{triv}}:(\mathcal{D}B)(L(s),P_L(s))\equiv0\right\}.
$$

Then

$$
|T_{\mathrm{triv}}|\le D,
\qquad
|T_{\mathrm{deg}}|\le D(D-1),
$$

and every $L\in T\setminus(T_{\mathrm{triv}}\cup T_{\mathrm{deg}})$ satisfies

$$
\left|\{x\in N_G(L):(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0\}\right|\le D.
$$

Consequently, for

$$
E_{\mathrm{exc}}=
\left\{(x,L)\in E:L\in T_{\mathrm{triv}}\cup T_{\mathrm{deg}}
\text{ or }(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0\right\},
$$

one has

$$
|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+Dt.
$$
lemmas.title: Exceptional-Root Cleanup

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Since every line vertex of $G$ has degree at least $k$,

$$
|E|\ge kt.
$$

Using P5 and the bound $D^2\le16384dt/k$ from P3 gives

$$
\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}
\le\frac{pD^2+Dt}{|E|}
\le\frac{D}{k}+\frac{16384dp}{k^2}
<\frac1{4000}.
$$

During peeling, each removed vertex accounts for fewer than $k_1$ edges present at its removal. The original minimum-degree condition on both vertex classes gives

$$
k(|X|+t)\le2|E|.
$$

Thus peeling removes fewer than

$$
k_1(|X|+t)
\le2\frac{k_1}{k}|E|
\le\frac{|E|}{50}
$$

additional edges. Together with the exceptional-edge bound, this is less than $|E|$, so at least one edge remains. The remaining graph has minimum degree at least $k_1$ by construction. It need not remain connected and may split into several components.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P5,

$$
\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}
\le\frac{D}{k}+\frac{16384dp}{k^2}
<\frac1{4000}.
$$

Set

$$
k_1=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{100}\right\rfloor.
$$

Starting from $(X,T,E\setminus E_{\mathrm{exc}})$ and iteratively deleting every vertex whose current degree is less than $k_1$ removes fewer than

$$
k_1(|X|+t)
\le2\frac{k_1}{k}|E|
\le\frac{|E|}{50}
$$

additional edges and leaves a nonempty subgraph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.
lemmas.title: Clean Core

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The numerical hypotheses give $k_1\ge2$. Fix $x\in X_1$ and choose two distinct incident lines $L_1,L_2\in T_1$. Their direction vectors $v_1,v_2$ are linearly independent, since two distinct affine lines through one point have distinct directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^2$.

Choose parametrizations $L_i(s)=x+sv_i$. Differentiating the formal identities

$$
B(L_i(s),P_{L_i}(s))\equiv0
$$

at $s=0$ gives

$$
v_{i,X}B_X(x,f(x))+v_{i,Y}B_Y(x,f(x))
+B_Z(x,f(x))P_{L_i}'(0)=0
$$

for $i\in\{1,2\}$. If $B_Z(x,f(x))=0$, the independence of $v_1$ and $v_2$ forces

$$
B_X(x,f(x))=B_Y(x,f(x))=0.
$$

All three formal partial derivatives would then vanish at $(x,f(x))$, implying $(\mathcal{D}B)(x,f(x))=0$. This contradicts the deletion rule defining $G_1$. Hence $B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$. No derivative of a line polynomial is divided by in this argument.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ be the surviving graph from P6, and let $B$ and $\mathcal{D}$ be as in P5. Then every $x\in X_1$ satisfies

$$
B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad
B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.
$$
lemmas.title: Simple Roots

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Choose any connected component $C$ of $G_1$. Its minimum degree is at least $k_1$, and the numerical bounds give $k_1>D$. KTZ Lemmas 2.7 and 6.1 lift the line roots through one point of $C$ to a single polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$. Every division in the Newton lift is by a value $B_Z(b,f(b))$, which is a nonzero field element by P7; all global polynomials produced by the lift retain total degree at most $d$.

Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same $Q$ throughout $C$, as in KTZ Lemma 6.3, without a factor-count loss. Thus $Q(x)=f(x)$ at every point vertex of $C$.

The first numerical hypothesis also implies

$$
\frac1{\sqrt{p+1}}\le\frac{k_1}{4p}.
$$

Applying the mixing argument of KTZ Lemma 6.2 to $C$ gives

$$
\frac{|X_C|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k_1}{4p}\ge\frac{k}{800p}.
$$

Since $Q=f$ on $X_C$, this is the asserted global agreement.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Under the hypotheses and notation of P1–P7, there exists a polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.
$$
lemmas.title: Polynomial Decoder

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The threshold implies that the pruned minimum-degree parameter satisfies

$$
k_0\ge\frac{\epsilon p}{200}.
$$

Squaring the threshold gives

$$
\epsilon^2p\ge8{,}000{,}000C_*\Lambda d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
k_0^2\ge C_*dp
$$

and

$$
k_0^3\ge C_*d(\Lambda\epsilon)p^2\ge C_*d\tau p^2.
$$

The component decoder established in P1–P8 therefore applies with $k=k_0$ and yields

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]
\ge\frac{k_0}{800p}
\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.
$$

This is the square-root parameter calculation. The entry remains conditional because local agreement alone has not supplied the assumed component with $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let

$$
\epsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],
$$

where $L$ is uniform among all affine lines of $\mathbb{F}_p^2$ and $x$ is uniform on $L$. Let $G_0$ be a graph supplied by KTZ Lemma 3.1 with minimum degree at least

$$
k_0=\left\lfloor\frac{\epsilon p}{100}\right\rfloor.
$$

Let $\Lambda\ge1$, and suppose $G_0$ has a connected component of line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$. Put $C_*=2^{40}$ and assume

$$
\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000C_*\Lambda}\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

Then there exists $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.
$$
lemmas.title: Small-Component Corollary

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Independently color every point and every affine line uniformly from $[K]$, and choose an injection $\iota:[K]\hookrightarrow\mathbb{F}_p$. Set $f(x)$ equal to the embedded color of $x$, and let $P_L$ be the constant embedded color of $L$.

Conditional on a vertex color, the accepted degree of a line has distribution

$$
\operatorname{Bin}\!\left(p,\frac1K\right),
$$

while the accepted degree of a point has distribution

$$
\operatorname{Bin}\!\left(p+1,\frac1K\right).
$$

A Chernoff bound and a union bound over fewer than $3p^2$ vertices show that the probability of any asserted degree bound failing is at most

$$
6p^2e^{-p/(12K)}<1,
$$

where the last inequality follows from $p/K\ge100\log p$. Hence a deterministic realization satisfying every degree bound exists. Averaging the line-degree bounds and dividing by $p$ gives the stated interval for $\epsilon$. Every $P_L$ has degree $0$, hence degree at most the campaign degree $d>100$; the construction does not assert a separate analysis of the excluded parameter choice $d=0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p\ge103$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $K$ be an integer satisfying

$$
2\le K\le\frac{p}{100\log p}.
$$

There exist a function $f:\mathbb{F}_p^2\to\mathbb{F}_p$ and a constant polynomial $P_L$ on every affine line $L$ such that, with

$$
\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L)=|\{x\in L:P_L(x)=f(x)\}|
$$

and

$$
\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(x)=|\{L\ni x:P_L(x)=f(x)\}|,
$$

one has, for every affine line $L$ and every point $x$,

$$
\frac{p}{2K}\le\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L)\le\frac{2p}{K},
$$

$$
\frac{p+1}{2K}\le\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(x)\le\frac{2(p+1)}{K}.
$$

The test agreement satisfies

$$
\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K.
$$
lemmas.title: Balanced-Color Realization

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The line-degree upper bound gives

$$
|S_R|\le\sum_{M\in R}\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(M)
\le\frac{2p|R|}{K}.
$$

The covering hypothesis and the line-degree lower bound imply that every affine line contributes at least $p/(4K)$ accepted incidences from $S_R$. Summing over all $p(p+1)$ affine lines gives at least

$$
\frac{p^2(p+1)}{4K}
$$

such incidences. On the other hand, the point-degree upper bound permits at most $2(p+1)/K$ accepted incidences per point of $S_R$. Therefore

$$
|S_R|\ge\frac{p^2}{8}.
$$

Combining the two estimates yields $|R|\ge Kp/16$. Since P10 gives $\epsilon\ge1/(2K)$,

$$
\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon}.
$$

Finally, $f$ assumes at most $K$ color values. By pigeonhole, one constant value occurs on at least a $1/K$ fraction of all points. The corresponding constant polynomial has agreement at least $1/K\ge\epsilon/2$, using the upper bound $\epsilon\le2/K$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $f$ and the line table be as in P10. For a set $R$ of affine lines, define

$$
S_R=\{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2:\exists\,M\in R\text{ with }x\in M\text{ and }P_M(x)=f(x)\}.
$$

Suppose that every affine line $L$ satisfies

$$
\left|S_R\cap\{x\in L:P_L(x)=f(x)\}\right|
\ge\frac12\deg_{\mathrm{acc}}(L).
$$

Then

$$
|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon}.
$$

Moreover, there exists a constant polynomial $Q\in\mathbb{F}_p[X,Y]$ such that

$$
\Pr_{x\in\mathbb{F}_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac1K\ge\frac{\epsilon}{2}.
$$
lemmas.title: Covering Lower Bound
